basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 24.' and it opens 'Vers. 24. Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain; de Lamech vero septuagies septies. Crescente'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 24. Septuplum ultio dabitur de Cain; de Lamech vero septuagies septies. Crescente peccato crescit | et ultio. Fuerunt autem septuaginta septem animae de stirpe Lamech quas in diluvio legimus periisse. Allegorice Lamech figuram tenet mundi hujus, cujus tantum fuit peccatum praevaricante Adam ut non posset expiari nisi septuagesima septima generatione, Christo per Virginem veniente.
